newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Nokia drops in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Nokia drops in New York.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Finland's Nokia Group fell on Thursday after the telecommunications company reported 1996 results.
A trader reported quiet trade in most European ADRS.
"The markets picked up on the back of the 100-point move (by the Dow industrials on Wednesday) but are shaky on fear that there will be a shakeout here," he said.

Nokia fell 3-5/8 to 63-1/2 after the company reported a 21 percent drop in profits, in line with analysts' expectations. Nokia was among the most active ADRs in late-morning trade, with 1.5 million shares traded.
A trader said the shares might have been affected by a rumor that Goldman Sachs had downgraded the stock. A spokesman for the brokerage said it had not changed Nokia's ratings.
Shares in Royal Dutch/Shell Group jumped after the oil giant announced record annual profits and a share split.
Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose 4-1/2 to 183-3/4 and Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc was up 2-3/8 to 106-1/2.

Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone holding Telebras rose 1-1/2 to 95 on positive sentiment for privatization. ING Barings set a 12-month price target for the ADR of $130 to $150, up from its previous target of $110 to 115.

Level One ADRs in Russian oil producer OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil LKOH.RTS O#LKOH.RUO preferred shares started trade in New York with bid price of $25.25 and an ask price of $26.25. The Level One ADRs trade over the counter on the OTC Bulletin Board.

A senior LUKoil executive said the company would sell 15 percent of government-owned stock in the form of ADRs by the end of the year. However, Loren Bough, a trader at New York's Brunswick Securities, said the announcement "was not news to the market."
Advancers led decliners by 280 to 199 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 45 million shares by midday.
